descriptionChirho: To bind or fasten something (a sword, belt, sackcloth, ephod, or other garment/weapon) around the waist or body of oneself or another person, including all active, imperative, imperfect, perfect, infinitive, and active participial forms of the primary root חגר I.

The state of being girded or having something fastened around oneself, expressed through passive/stative participial forms describing someone as currently wearing or equipped with a belt, sackcloth, sword, linen ephod, or similar item.

A separate homographic root חגר II meaning to tremble, shudder, or come out in trembling fear, attested in prophetic contexts (cf. Micah 7:17, Hosea 11:10-11) where the sense is clearly distinct from girding.
